entries.text: One-time login — a long-lived per-device token (localStorage) silently re-issues the session on every visit, so the device never asks for credentials again.
No login flash — already signed in? You're sent straight to the dashboard instead of the login form.
Show/hide password toggle on every password field — sign-in, registration, profile change-password, and the admin create/edit user modals.
Logout now revokes the device token server-side — signing out anywhere is a real sign-out, not just a cleared session cookie.
The Cabinet — a playful new /tools hub in the navbar hosts Catarina's tools as cards, each with its own color and tagline.
Drawers — a shared team workspace per section: chests, projects, envelopes and loose files, synced instantly to the team cloud.
Chunked uploads — large files split into small parts and reassembled in storage, so anything fits without platform limits.
Team Tables — a free-form grid per section: add & delete rows and columns, merge a selection, split merged cells back.
Date mode — mark dates and Catarina lights up today's whole column (or row) in the table's accent color.
Rina stickers — drop character stickers on any table; they dance, and you can pause, tilt, drag, lock and mirror them.
Themed PDF export — print a table dark or light, portrait or landscape (or let Catarina auto-fit), stickers optional.
Manage Team Tables permission — a new per-member flag (on by default); admins always bypass it, everyone else reads.
Accessibility — drawers and the table editor ship with keyboard focus, focus traps, and clear element roles.
Housekeeping — removed the standalone features showcase page and tidied dev scaffolding; README, changelog, and docs updated.
Replaced Upstash Redis with Turso — rate limiting now lives in the same database Catarina already uses. One less service to keep alive.
True sliding-window limiter with atomic batch transactions — attempts stay counted across every Vercel cold start.
Self-cleaning rate-limit table and fail-open behavior — brute-force protection that can't pause, archive, or 500 the app.
Added 7 unit tests covering window boundaries, aging, and per-key isolation, plus a production migration run.
Section data isolation — members can only see goals in their assigned sections.
Admin checks re-verified against the database — token roles can no longer be forged.
Fail-fast auth — the app refuses to start without a JWT_SECRET.
Self-demotion and last-admin protection — admins can't lock themselves or the team out.
Data-loss guard — users who authored goals can't be deleted until goals are reassigned.
Stricter input validation across admin sections, registration, and profile endpoints.
Duplicate email on approval now returns a clean error instead of crashing.
Fixed a transient duplicate goal on creation and cleaned up dead code.
Added 30 unit tests for goal merging, permissions, and shared utilities.
Deploy your own Catarina — added NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL env var for SEO, sitemap, and OpenGraph.
Dynamic web manifest — PWA branding now reads from environment variables.
Team-agnostic seed script — new deployments get generic demo goals, no hardcoded content.
Upstash Redis rate limiting — brute-force protection now works across Vercel cold starts.
Proper Prisma migration workflow — added db:migrate, db:deploy, db:status scripts.
README overhaul — platform links, Catarina stickers, and complete deploy guide.
Removed all hardcoded branding — app is now fully white-label configurable.
New NotificationModal — tap any notification to see full details, goal data, changelog entries, and deep-link to goals.
Goal highlight on deep link — navigating from a notification scrolls to the goal and pulses it with the section color.
Styled assignee checkboxes as toggle pills, custom select dropdowns, and section-colored month picker.
Security hardening — removed hardcoded JWT fallback secret, added rate limiting on auth endpoints.
Removed dead dependencies (recharts, jspdf) and dead components. Converted login/404 to Server Components.
Added aria-live regions to stats bar, goal cards, and notification badges for screen reader updates.
Migrated middleware to Next.js 16 proxy convention to fix deprecation warning.
Scrollbar hover glow now works in all browsers — both main app and modal scrollbars glow on hover.
Fixed PDF export print styling so page background and inner padding render consistently.
Added new Catarina notification stickers for goal creation, deadline alerts, comments, system updates, and role changes.
Polished responsive dashboard and mobile navbar/report UI behavior.
Bumped version to 0.4.1 and synchronized release notes.
Real-time change detection — changes from other users appear within 5s without page reload
Delta fetching — only modified data is transferred, not full page reloads
Smart polling — adjusts interval based on tab visibility and user activity
Optimistic mutations — your actions appear instantly, with rollback on failure
Goal glow animation — new goals from other users shimmer with a subtle teal glow
Section pulse — dashboard cards pulse when goals change in that section
Toast notifications — incoming changes trigger a brief toast in the navbar
Static asset caching — rina images, pfps, and fonts now have infinite browser cache
Service worker v3 — precaches static assets, network-first for dashboard pages
Component extraction — DonutChart, SectionDetail, EditUserModal, CreateUserModal, PfpUpload split from monolithic files
Custom hooks — useCountUp, useFileUpload for shared logic
Shared type system — GoalData, SectionData, UserData centralized in src/types
Loading skeleton states for dashboard, section, and admin pages
Accessibility — checkbox roles, aria-checked, prefers-reduced-motion
Lint cleanup — 39 issues resolved (39 → 1, remaining is dev script only)
SEO sitemap generation via src/app/sitemap.ts
Update celebration system — you'll now see what's new after each release
Tiered celebration modals for major, minor, and patch updates
In-app changelog — tap the notification to see what changed
Edit your name, email, bio, profile photo, and password
Catarina character expressions throughout the app
Welcome celebration modal for first-time users
Comment notifications — section members are now notified
Bug fixes and UI polish across the board
Initial release — full team planning and tracking system
Monthly goal tracking with sections, steps, and comments
Live performance dashboard with animated charts
In-app notification system with pinning and audio
Archive & PDF export for completed months
Progressive Web App — installable on any device

0.7.0.title: Security Hardening — Headers, CSRF & Rate Limits

entries.text: Security headers on every response — strict CSP (script-src self + inline, no remote/eval), frame-ancestors block, nosniff, DENY, strict-origin-when-cross-origin, and HSTS with preload in production.
Same-origin edge guard — every mutating /api call (POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE) from the wrong Origin now answers 403 before it reaches the handler; the HttpOnly cookie stays SameSite=Lax.
Rate limited auth — login, register, password change, refresh and logout are each throttled to 10 requests/minute per IP (429 beyond that), grinding the public auth surface.
Weak-secret boot warning — a short or guessable JWT_SECRET is surfaced loudly at startup (still fails hard if it's missing entirely) so a dev never ships with a forgeable token.

Dependencies — Next.js patched to 16.3.6, clearing the critical unauthenticated RCE plus the sharp/libvips, postcss and nanoid advisories. Prisma stays 7.x (the audit's suggested 'fix' was only a downgrade).
Audited every route and input — no untrusted data reaches eval, no origin bypasses the guard, and hashed refresh tokens plus HttpOnly cookies and granular per-section permissions hold the line.

Rate-limit bypass closed — login is capped at 10 attempts/15min per account on top of 10/min per IP, register at 3/5min per account and per IP, and a forged IP header can no longer hand you a fresh bucket. That 15 minutes is now genuinely enforced too, not quietly cut short.
The limiter no longer fails open — if the database hiccups, requests fall back to a bounded in-memory counter instead of sailing through.
Login no longer leaks which emails exist — every attempt costs exactly one password comparison, so response time can't be used to enumerate accounts.
A null Origin can no longer slip past the CSRF guard — any origin that is present but invalid is rejected instead of trusted.
Refresh tokens now rotate and work once — a stolen token is good for a single refresh before it is burned, reuse signs the whole session family out, and every family ends 30 days after sign-in.

Uploaded drawer files can no longer run as pages — whether a file previews inline is decided by its actual bytes, never by its name or declared type, and everything else downloads with sniffing disabled.
Team tables stopped eating each other's edits — two people editing the same table now get asked to merge instead of one silently overwriting the other.
Signing up can no longer take over an existing account — a repeat signup is refused with one uniform message, and admins can clear an old request so that person can try again.
Passwords need 8+ characters and can't be one of the usual leaked ones — checked whenever you set a new password, so nobody with an older password is locked out.
